scope: The five actually imported JSON-schema builder distributions and rpds Rust source/build closure are external build inputs. Separately, exact observed Rust standard-library copies in the already-shipped cryptography and pydantic-core extensions are runtime embedded attribution components. No application dependency is added.
evidence_limits: Artifact payloads were not executed from the download cache or source archives. Original installed developer-environment wheel files were compared as bytes; offline review QA uses the already-installed builder. This does not certify unrelated environment files or a clean-machine build.

The rpds vendor CycloneDX document declares all_targets=true: 15 required and 2 excluded crate entries. Source Cargo.lock adds portable-atomic under the PyO3 target condition not(target_has_atomic=64). All 18 records are retained as source/build provenance without claiming all are linked into the Windows extension.
The rpds package is consumed as its exact prebuilt wheel. Upstream maturin, pytest, documentation, typing and developer-only dependency groups are not asserted executed builder tools.

Rust system runtime identities come from exact commit markers embedded in each hash-verified selected native extension. No human release version, full compiler execution provenance, exact linked-object list or all-targets compilation is inferred.

The Windows std source manifests establish cfg-if/hashbrown/rustc-demangle and in-tree compiler-builtins/backtrace provenance. Optional non-Windows std libraries, test crates, compiler backends and optional host C build-tool ancestry are not asserted runtime components.

Immutable upstream license-metadata and REUSE records are preserved as source evidence. The normalized Windows attribution excludes the Fuchsia-only mutex notice; source-evidence text may discuss unrelated compiler platforms and is not a claim those are shipped.
